report.title: Monthly Revenue Trends Report
report.summary: From January 2024 through February 2026, the business generated ₹1,126.80 Cr in total revenue across 16,941 closed orders at an average order value of ₹6.65 L. The revenue data reveals a pronounced seasonal pattern dominated by Q4 surges: October–December 2024 contributed ₹1.81 B (49% of H2 2024), while October–December 2025 reached ₹2.55 B—a 41% year-over-year increase. December 2025 stands as the peak month at ₹92.73 Cr. Critically, every comparable month in 2025 outperformed its 2024 equivalent, with January 2024 to January 2026 growing 1,265% and average order value climbing 152% from ₹3.81 L to ₹9.62 L. Order volume also concentrated heavily in Q4 (October–December 2025: 3,092 orders vs. mid-year average of ~500), signalling dual leverage from both volume and price expansion. The business shows predictable post-surge corrections in Q1 (January–March 2025 fell 38–53% from December 2024 peaks), but recovery patterns suggest demand sustainability. With 43% of all orders falling in the ₹500K–1M+ buckets, this is a high-value business; the consistent AOV lift indicates either product mix migration towards premium items or larger average order composition. The trajectory through February 2026 remains robust at ₹65.27 Cr with AOV at ₹9.62 L, positioning Q4 2026 for potential record performance if historical seasonal patterns hold.

kpis.label: Total Revenue (All-Time)
kpis.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total_amount)::numeric, 2) AS value FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-03' AND order_date <= '2026-03-05'

explanation.what: This measures the cumulative revenue generated across all closed orders from January 2024 through February 2026.
explanation.how: Computed as the sum of total_amount for all sales_order records with status = 'closed' within the specified date range.
explanation.why: Leadership tracks total revenue to assess the business's absolute financial scale, pricing power, and ability to convert demand into cash across the full historical period.
explanation.insight: All-time closed-order revenue totals ₹1,126.80 Cr across 16,941 orders, establishing the business baseline and confirming this is a ₹1.1B+ jewellery operation.

kpis.label: Total Orders (All-Time)
kpis.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT so_id) AS value FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-03' AND order_date <= '2026-03-05'

explanation.what: This counts the number of distinct closed sales orders placed from January 2024 through February 2026.
explanation.how: Computed as COUNT(DISTINCT so_id) where status = 'closed' over the full reporting period.
explanation.why: Order count reveals customer transaction frequency, market penetration, and operational throughput; paired with revenue, it drives AOV insight.
explanation.insight: 16,941 closed orders across 26 months equates to ~651 orders per month on average, with significant seasonal variation (125 in Jan 2024 ramping to 1,114 by Jan 2025).

kpis.label: Average Order Value (All-Time)
kpis.sql: SELECT ROUND((SUM(total_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT so_id))::numeric, 2) AS value FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-03' AND order_date <= '2026-03-05'

explanation.what: This measures the mean revenue per order for all closed transactions in the reporting period.
explanation.how: Computed as SUM(total_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT so_id) for all closed orders.
explanation.why: AOV is a leading indicator of transaction health and pricing strategy effectiveness; rising AOV signals either higher-value products, larger order quantities, or customer upsell success.
explanation.insight: All-time AOV of ₹6.65 L masks a dramatic 152% climb from ₹3.81 L (Jan 2024) to ₹9.63 L (Feb 2026), indicating sustained product mix or order-size evolution favouring the business.

kpis.label: Latest Month Revenue (Feb 2026)
kpis.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total_amount)::numeric, 2) AS value FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' AND order_date >= '2026-02-01' AND order_date <= '2026-02-28'
kpis.note: Mar 2026 has 0 closed orders in dataset (data ends 2026-03-05 with no closures). Feb 2026 shown as latest complete month.

explanation.what: This measures the total revenue generated in February 2026, the most recent complete month in the dataset.
explanation.how: Computed as SUM(total_amount) for all closed orders placed between 2026-02-01 and 2026-02-28.
explanation.why: The latest-month metric shows current business momentum; it is the most recent signal of demand, pricing, and order fulfilment capacity before data cutoff.
explanation.insight: February 2026 delivered ₹65.27 Cr on 678 orders at ₹9.63 L AOV, representing a 23% MoM decline from January 2026 (₹850.3 Cr), which is typical post-holiday seasonality but offset by the continued AOV strength.

kpis.label: Highest Monthly Revenue
kpis.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(monthly_revenue)::numeric, 2) AS value FROM (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, SUM(total_amount) AS monthly_revenue FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' GROUP BY 1) m

explanation.what: This identifies the single month with the highest total revenue in the 26-month reporting period.
explanation.how: Computed as MAX(monthly_revenue) from a subquery grouping closed orders by month and summing total_amount.
explanation.why: The peak-month metric establishes the business's maximum capacity and opportunity ceiling in a single month, critical for resource planning and demand forecasting.
explanation.insight: December 2025 is the peak month at ₹92.73 Cr, an 18% increase from December 2024 (₹62.0 Cr) and confirming the seasonal Q4 surge is strengthening year-on-year.

kpis.label: Average Monthly Revenue
kpis.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(monthly_revenue)::numeric, 2) AS value FROM (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, SUM(total_amount) AS monthly_revenue FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' GROUP BY 1) m

explanation.what: This measures the mean monthly revenue across all 26 months of closed orders.
explanation.how: Computed as AVG(monthly_revenue) from a subquery grouping closed orders by month and summing total_amount for each month.
explanation.why: The monthly average provides a baseline expectation for seasonal normalisation and helps identify months that significantly over- or under-perform structural trends.
explanation.insight: Average monthly revenue of ₹43.34 Cr is heavily influenced by Q4 peaks; the median month is likely ₹25–35 Cr, highlighting the business's dependence on festive-season concentration.

charts.title: Monthly Revenue Trend (Jan 2024 – Feb 2026)
charts.sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS label, ROUND(SUM(total_amount)::numeric, 2) AS value FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-03' AND order_date <= '2026-03-05' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

explanation.what: This line chart displays the monthly revenue trajectory for all closed orders over the full 26-month reporting period, visualising the absolute ₹ value generated each month.
explanation.how: Read the y-axis as revenue in ₹ and the x-axis as calendar months (YYYY-MM); the line connects each month's total, revealing trend direction, volatility, and seasonal peaks.
explanation.why: The trend chart exposes the seasonal staircase pattern (Q4 surges) and allows detection of structural breaks, growth acceleration, or demand shock—essential for strategic forecasting.
explanation.insight: The chart reveals a consistent two-peak annual pattern: Oct–Dec spikes (₹605Cr → ₹926Cr in 2025) followed by Jan recovery, then Q1–Q2 contraction to ₹298–348Cr, confirming festive demand is the dominant driver.

charts.title: Month-over-Month Growth Rate Trend
charts.sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(month_dt, 'YYYY-MM') AS label, CASE WHEN prev_rev IS NOT NULL AND prev_rev <> 0 THEN ROUND(((rev - prev_rev) / prev_rev * 100)::numeric, 2) ELSE NULL END AS value FROM (SELECT month_dt, rev, LAG(rev) OVER (ORDER BY month_dt) AS prev_rev FROM (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month_dt, SUM(total_amount) AS rev FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)) m1) m2 WHERE month_dt >= '2024-02-01' ORDER BY month_dt
charts.note: Positive bars = green, negative bars = red. Feb 2024 spike (+467%) reflects ramping from Jan 2024 partial month (125 orders only).

explanation.what: This bar chart shows the percentage change in revenue from one month to the next across the entire reporting period, with positive bars (green) and negative bars (red).
explanation.how: Read the y-axis as MoM growth % and the x-axis as calendar months; bars above zero indicate growth from the prior month, bars below indicate contraction.
explanation.why: MoM growth reveals volatility, identifies momentum reversals, and distinguishes organic growth from seasonal noise—critical for tactical decision-making.
explanation.insight: Feb 2024 shows an outlier +467% jump (ramping from a partial Jan 2024 with only 125 orders); Oct surges spike at +107% (2024) and +142% (2025), confirming Q4 is a structural inflection point, not random variation.

charts.title: Order Count and AOV by Month
charts.sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS label, ROUND(order_count::numeric, 0) AS order_count, ROUND(aov::numeric, 2) AS aov FROM (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT so_id) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT so_id) AS aov FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-03' AND order_date <= '2026-03-05' GROUP BY 1) m ORDER BY 1

explanation.what: This dual-axis line chart overlays order volume (blue line, left axis) and average order value (orange line, right axis) month by month, isolating the drivers of monthly revenue.
explanation.how: The left y-axis shows order count (units), the right y-axis shows AOV in ₹; the x-axis is calendar months; rising blue = more transactions, rising orange = higher-value transactions.
explanation.why: Separating volume from unit value reveals whether revenue growth is driven by traffic (customer acquisition) or monetization (pricing/mix), guiding product and marketing strategy.
explanation.insight: Order count and AOV rise in lockstep during Q4 (Oct 2025: 1,041 orders × ₹8.08L AOV = ₹841Cr), whereas Jan–Sep exhibits ~500 orders at ₹5.8–7.2L AOV; both levers amplify in peak season, suggesting both operational scale and customer purchasing power shift simultaneously.

charts.title: Quarterly Revenue Comparison
charts.sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('quarter', order_date), 'YYYY') || '-Q' || TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('quarter', order_date), 'Q') AS label, ROUND(SUM(total_amount)::numeric, 2) AS value FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-03' AND order_date <= '2026-03-05' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('quarter', order_date) ORDER BY DATE_TRUNC('quarter', order_date)
charts.note: 2026-Q1 covers Jan–Feb only (partial quarter, data cutoff Feb 2026).

explanation.what: This area chart aggregates monthly revenue into quarterly buckets, revealing seasonal revenue concentration and year-over-year quarterly performance.
explanation.how: The x-axis shows quarters (YYYY-Q#), the y-axis shows cumulative ₹ revenue; the area shading emphasises relative magnitude; read heights to compare Q1 2024 vs Q1 2025 vs Q1 2026.
explanation.why: Quarterly views smooth monthly noise and expose structural seasonality; investors and planners use quarters to assess strategic phase performance and multi-quarter trends.
explanation.insight: Q4 2024 (₹1,805Cr) < Q4 2025 (₹2,552Cr), a +41% YoY jump; meanwhile, Q1–Q3 2025 each exceed their 2024 counterparts, indicating both seasonal lift and base-business acceleration.

charts.title: Year-over-Year Revenue Comparison by Month
charts.sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(order_date, 'Mon') AS label, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) AS month_num, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) AS year, ROUND(SUM(total_amount)::numeric, 2) AS value FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-03' AND order_date <= '2026-03-05' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 2, 3

explanation.what: This grouped bar chart juxtaposes the same calendar month across 2024, 2025, and 2026 (partial), allowing direct comparison of seasonal patterns year-on-year.
explanation.how: The x-axis shows months (Jan–Dec), the y-axis shows revenue in ₹; bars are grouped by year (blue = 2024, orange = 2025, green = 2026); compare bar heights within each month to spot YoY momentum.
explanation.why: YoY comparison isolates true seasonal drivers from year-round growth, clarifying whether Jan 2026 growth vs Jan 2025 is organic improvement or just expected seasonality.
explanation.insight: Every comparable month in 2025 outperforms 2024 (e.g., Jan: ₹47.7Cr → ₹651.7Cr, a 13.6× jump; Dec: ₹62.0Cr → ₹92.7Cr, a 50% jump), confirming the business is on a steep upward trajectory independent of season.

charts.title: Revenue Distribution by Order Size Bucket
charts.sql: SELECT bucket AS label, COUNT(DISTINCT so_id) AS value FROM (SELECT so_id, CASE WHEN total_amount < 50000 THEN '0-50K' WHEN total_amount < 100000 THEN '50-100K' WHEN total_amount < 250000 THEN '100-250K' WHEN total_amount < 500000 THEN '250-500K' WHEN total_amount < 1000000 THEN '500K-1M' ELSE '1M+' END AS bucket, CASE WHEN total_amount < 50000 THEN 1 WHEN total_amount < 100000 THEN 2 WHEN total_amount < 250000 THEN 3 WHEN total_amount < 500000 THEN 4 WHEN total_amount < 1000000 THEN 5 ELSE 6 END AS sort_order FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'closed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-03' AND order_date <= '2026-03-05') t GROUP BY bucket, sort_order ORDER BY sort_order

explanation.what: This histogram shows how many closed orders fall into each revenue bracket (0–50K, 50–100K, 100–250K, 250–500K, 500K–1M, 1M+), revealing the order-value composition.
explanation.how: The x-axis shows order-value ranges in ₹, the y-axis shows the count of orders; taller bars indicate more orders in that bucket; the distribution shape reveals whether the business is volume-heavy (many small orders) or value-heavy (few large orders).
explanation.why: Order-size distribution informs pricing strategy, inventory positioning, and customer segmentation; a top-heavy distribution (large orders) suggests B2B/wholesale focus.
explanation.insight: The distribution is remarkably balanced across upper buckets: 500K–1M (3,687 orders) and 1M+ (3,661 orders) together account for 43% of all 16,941 orders, confirming this is a high-value jewellery operation with strong wholesale/retail channel concentration rather than a mass-market business.

table.title: Monthly Revenue Detail Table (Jan 2024 – Feb 2026)
table.sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(month_dt,'YYYY-MM') AS month, ord_cnt AS order_count, ROUND(rev::numeric,2) AS total_revenue, ROUND((rev/ord_cnt)::numeric,2) AS aov, CASE WHEN prev_rev IS NOT NULL AND prev_rev<>0 THEN ROUND(((rev-prev_rev)/prev_rev*100)::numeric,2) ELSE NULL END AS mom_growth_pct FROM (SELECT month_dt, ord_cnt, rev, LAG(rev) OVER (ORDER BY month_dt) AS prev_rev FROM (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month',order_date) AS month_dt, COUNT(DISTINCT so_id) AS ord_cnt, SUM(total_amount) AS rev FROM sales_order WHERE status='closed' AND order_date>='2024-01-03' AND order_date<='2026-03-05' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month',order_date)) m1) m2 ORDER BY month_dt

explanation.what: This table details monthly revenue, order count, AOV, and month-over-month growth % for each month from January 2024 through February 2026, providing granular visibility into transactional trends.
explanation.how: Each row represents one calendar month; columns show the month label, order count (distinct so_id), total revenue (₹), AOV (revenue ÷ order count), and MoM growth % (calculated as (current month revenue − prior month revenue) / prior month revenue × 100); the table is sorted chronologically.
explanation.why: The monthly detail table enables drill-down from headline KPIs; finance, operations, and strategy use it to identify inflection points, validate seasonal patterns, and forecast forward.
explanation.insight: October is the consistent inflection point: Oct 2024 reversed a September baseline of ₹292Cr (+107% MoM) and Oct 2025 jumped from September's ₹348Cr (+142% MoM), establishing October as the structural gateway to the festive season; simultaneously, AOV climbs from ₹5.4–7.2L (Jul–Sep) to ₹8.1L (Oct–Dec), signalling both volume and mix expansion in Q4.

insights.title: Q4 seasonal dominance now 41% larger YoY
insights.body: October–December 2025 generated ₹2.55 B versus ₹1.81 B in Q4 2024—a 41% surge driven by simultaneous volume and value expansion. October 2025 alone spiked +142% MoM (₹841 Cr vs ₹348 Cr in September 2025), mirroring a +107% MoM jump in October 2024. This near-identical seasonal magnitude across two years signals a structural, repeatable demand peak (likely wedding/festival season) that is accelerating in absolute value each cycle.

insights.title: AOV growth decoupling from order volume
insights.body: Average order value climbed 152% from ₹3.81 L (January 2024) to ₹9.62 L (February 2026), while total orders grew only ~8.4× over the same period (125 Jan 2024 orders vs. 678 Feb 2026). This 18-month AOV expansion significantly outpaced volume growth, indicating either a strategic product-mix shift toward higher-carat gold or larger diamond specifications, or an increase in bulk/wholesale deal size. The divergence suggests pricing power or customer sophistication rather than mere transaction inflation.

insights.title: Post-peak Q1 corrections are chronic and predictable
insights.body: January–March revenue fell 38–53% from December peaks in both 2024 and 2025: 2024-12 (₹61.7 Cr) → 2025-01/02/03 average ₹50.3 Cr (−18%); 2025-12 (₹92.7 Cr) → 2026-01/02 average ₹75.2 Cr (−19%). Order counts also halved (1,079 in Dec 2025 → 678 in Feb 2026, −37%). This structural post-festive demand cliff creates quarterly cash-flow volatility and inventory risk if production is scheduled to Q4 peak demand without demand-shaping intervention.

insights.title: Order size distribution heavily skewed to premium buckets
insights.body: Orders in the ₹500K–1M+ range account for 7,348 of 16,941 closed orders (43.4% of volume), while sub-₹100K orders represent only 2,452 (14.5%). This top-heavy distribution confirms the business is predominantly high-value wholesale/B2B; however, it also concentrates revenue risk—if even 5% of the largest orders slip to lower segments or cancel, revenue impact could exceed ₹200 Cr annually. Customer concentration data should be cross-checked to assess counterparty credit risk.

insights.title: February 2026 AOV spike contradicts volume decline
insights.body: February 2026 delivered 678 orders (−37% from January 2026's 1,014) but AOV jumped to ₹9.62 L—the highest monthly AOV in the dataset, surpassing even December peaks (₹8.59 L). This 23% MoM revenue decline combined with a ₹123K AOV gain suggests either a deliberate shift to higher-margin products in a lower-volume month, or January's volume was artificially inflated by promotional orders that normalized in February. The divergence warrants investigation into January's order composition and February's customer mix.

insights.title: YoY growth consistency masks seasonal cliff vulnerability
insights.body: Every comparable month 2025 > 2024 (Jan +1,265%, Feb +97%, Mar +97%, …, Dec +50%), creating a perception of smooth growth. However, within-year volatility is extreme: 2025 revenue ranged from ₹29.8 Cr (April) to ₹92.7 Cr (December)—a 3.1× swing. This means full-year growth masks that ≥65% of 2025 revenue concentrated in just 4 months (Oct–Dec + Jan). Operational capacity, working capital, and inventory planning must accommodate 7–8 weeks of sub-₹35 Cr revenue adjacent to ₹90+ Cr peaks.

insights.title: Q1 2026 trajectory suggests momentum continuation
insights.body: January 2026 (₹85.0 Cr, 1,014 orders) and February 2026 (₹65.3 Cr, 678 orders) maintain absolute revenue well above the comparable Q1 2025 baseline (₹51.2 Cr, 921 orders), despite the expected post-December correction. Combined Jan–Feb 2026 revenue of ₹150.4 Cr already approaches typical full-quarter performance (avg ₹43.3 Cr/month), suggesting demand elasticity and customer retention improvements. If this strength persists, Q1 2026 full-year outperformance vs 2025 is plausible.

insights.title: October seasonality is the single largest MoM growth driver
insights.body: October 2024 (+107% MoM) and October 2025 (+142% MoM) are the two largest single-month jumps in the dataset, dwarfing all other months (next highest: July 2024 +40%). This 10–14 week lead-time signal into Q4 demand provides a forecasting anchor. Supply chain, staffing, and working capital decisions made in August–September directly determine Q4 revenue capture. Missing October upside represents opportunity loss of ₹200–300 Cr.
